## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to implement a deterministic, branchless byte-level permutation on a 128-bit value, a common pattern in low-level data encoding and hash-like transformations.

## Key Concepts

- Byte slicing and reassembly
- Unrolled, fixed permutations
- Inlining and branchless bit-twiddling

## Code Example

```c
// P is a 16-element permutation of {0..15}, evaluated at compile time
uint128 permuteBytes128(uint128 x) {
  return ( (x >> (8*0)) & 0xFF) << (8*P[0]) |
         ( (x >> (8*1)) & 0xFF) << (8*P[1]) |
         ...
         ( (x >> (8*15)) & 0xFF) << (8*P[15]);
}
```

}

## Why This Is Asked
Shows mastery of low-level bit tricks and edge-case handling in constrained environments.

## Key Concepts
- Next permutation with fixed popcount using bit hacks
- Branchless arithmetic for speed
- Fixed-width overflow behavior

## Code Example
```javascript
uint64_t nextHigherWithSamePopcount(uint64_t n) {
  uint64_t c = n & -n;
  uint64_t r = n + c;
  return (((n ^ r) >> 2) / c) | r;
}
```
